Test image shows a mango leaf with a white/cream powdery coating concentrated along the midrib and upper surface. The leaf is otherwise green, and the coating has a dusty, granular texture — classic powdery mildew appearance. No dark necrotic spots (anthracnose), no tip dieback, no black sooty coating.

Now checking one reference per class:
Good match — same dusty white/gray powdery patches across the leaf surface. Now checking the other three classes:

Clear comparison across all four classes:

- **Powdery_Mildew**: White dusty coating on green leaf — matches test image closely
- **Anthracnose**: Brown/tan leaf with dark necrotic lesions — no match
- **Die_Back**: Severely desiccated brown branch — no match
- **Sooty_Mould**: Dark/black patches on leaf — no match

The test image shows white powdery granular deposits concentrated along the midrib on an otherwise green leaf, which is the hallmark of powdery mildew.
